clue.text: Second wife has silver items stolen

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
W is the abbreviation for wife
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver, from Latin argentum

explanation.surface: A man's second wife turns out to have stolen silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: Swag is slang for a burglar's haul.
explanation.definitionFit: Swag is informal for loot, the goods a thief carries away.

clue.text: A single wicket defeat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the three upright posts of a cricket wicket
second meaning: baffle or outwit someone

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the wicket is three upright sticks, each one a stump. The surface suggests losing by one wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket post is one of the three pieces of a wicket, and to baffle someone completely is to beat them.

clue.text: Confused man, on about plucky mythological king

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters go around the other word
something confused is muddled up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters taken as written
game means brave and willing

explanation.surface: A bewildered man rambles on about a brave king of myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the king of Mycenae in Greek legend who led the Greeks against Troy.

clue.text: Sells fish in punts

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, wrapped by the outer word

parts.note: a punt is a gamble, so punts are wagers
a ray is a flat sea fish

explanation.surface: A fishmonger sells fish from flat-bottomed boats on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Punts looks like the river boats, but here it means gambles.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell someone out is to betray them, so sells works as a synonym for this verb.

clue.text: Radical, and bossy, initially, when in charge

indicators.note: initially points to the start of a word, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of bossy
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A description of a domineering leader: extreme and overbearing when running things.
explanation.walkthrough: Radical here means fundamental, from the root, not politically extreme.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical means going to the root, fundamental, which is a sense of the adjective basic.

clue.text: Savoury snacks brought in by Dermot, a pastrycook

indicators.note: the answer is carried inside the following words, which hold it within them

parts.note: found across the end of the name, the a, and the start of the last word

explanation.surface: A baker named Dermot delivers some savoury nibbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small Spanish appetisers served with drinks, i.e. savoury bites.

clue.text: Evergreen song about gold-topped automobile

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the song wraps around what follows

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
Au is the chemical symbol for gold; topped says it sits above the next piece in this down entry
a car is an automobile

explanation.surface: A sentimental ballad about a gold-roofed car.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold-topped places the gold on top of the car, which in a down clue means before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria is the genus of conifers including the monkey puzzle tree, which keeps its leaves all year.

clue.text: Win everything in lottery — bet hoard is put abroad

parts.note: a sweep is a sweepstake, a kind of lottery

indicators.note: something put abroad is scattered far and wide, so these letters land in a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A lottery winner's hoard of bets is sent overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from card games where one player takes every card on the table, so it means winning every prize.

clue.text: One may be employed in the kitchen

definitions.text: One may be employed in the kitchen

parts.words: One may be employed in the kitchen
parts.note: surface reading: a cook or scullery maid hired to work in a kitchen; setter's reading: employed means used, so this is an item put to use for drying dishes

explanation.walkthrough: Employed suggests a hired servant, but it simply means used: the answer is a cloth, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: This cloth is used in the kitchen to dry washed crockery and cutlery.

clue.text: Warriors scarred us badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that fighting men left them badly wounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusaders were the medieval Christian fighters who campaigned in the Holy Land.

clue.text: Attack report exposing credit arrangement

parts.note: to charge is to rush at, to attack
an account is a report or description of events

explanation.surface: A news report of an assault reveals some dodgy financial dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a customer facility at a shop that lets purchases be paid for later, i.e. buying on credit.

clue.text: One's run out of fish in square?

indicators.note: having run out of somewhere means having gone from it, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: plaice is a flatfish
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fishmonger in the town square has sold out of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The I leaves PLAICE to give PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A place is an open public area in a town, as in French street names, so it can mean a square.

clue.text: They're training strange caprine pets

indicators.note: something strange is odd and out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is training some odd pet goats.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprentices are learners bound to a skilled worker while they learn a trade, so they are people in training.

clue.text: Better clubs used by a professional, originally

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
taken as written

indicators.note: originally points to how a word starts, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of professional

explanation.surface: A golfer considers whether better clubs were originally used by a pro.
explanation.walkthrough: Better is a verb here, not an adjective describing clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap something is to outdo or top it, so it is a synonym of the verb better.

clue.text: Stayed well away from obese person on board who may have been …

definitions.meaning: first meaning: kept a safe distance from someone

definitions.text: obese person on board who may have been …
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a large passenger on a ship who was allotted a roomy bunk

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis invites you to finish the sentence; read literally, the phrase describes a large passenger allotted a generous bunk on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means avoided, originally a nautical phrase for keeping a ship clear of another at anchor.

clue.text: Beagle with vet injured lady's finger, say

indicators.note: something injured is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written; with simply joins them

explanation.surface: A beagle at the vet's has hurt a woman's finger.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady's finger is another name for okra, so 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra, also called lady's finger, is a green pod eaten as greens, so it is one example of this food class.

clue.text: Stream of abuse at bride, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or not right, so these letters are out of order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a torrent of insults was aimed at the bride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I suspect' reads as an aside, but the I is part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a tirade of angry criticism.

clue.text: Bishop, walking in the countryside, identifies a finch

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
rambling is walking for pleasure in the country

explanation.surface: A bishop out on a country walk spots a finch.
explanation.definitionFit: The brambling is a Eurasian bird of the finch family, a winter visitor to Britain.

clue.text: Careful not to hurt a man's beagle, last to be trained

indicators.note: a dog to be trained must be reshaped and disciplined, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog owner is told to handle his beagle tenderly, as it is the last to go to obedience classes.
explanation.definitionFit: The simile describes someone very mild and tender, as a lamb is proverbially meek and harmless.

clue.text: Lower score

definitions.meaning: first meaning: reduce, as with prices
second meaning: make an incision or a slash in

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a lower mark in a test; both words are separate verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to reduce an amount and to make a slit or incision in a surface.

clue.text: Personal souvenirs from Mobile, Maria sorted out

indicators.note: things sorted out are rearranged into a different order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Maria sorts through keepsakes from her time in Mobile, Alabama.
explanation.definitionFit: Memorabilia are objects kept for their association with people or events, i.e. keepsakes and mementos.

clue.text: Painter's long flowing hair beginning to thin

parts.note: a mane is a long thick head of hair

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of thin

explanation.surface: An artist's flowing locks are starting to thin.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a nineteenth-century French artist, a forerunner of Impressionism.

clue.text: Bike in gym inside Ministry of Defence

indicators.note: inside places one word within the letters of the other

parts.note: MoD is the abbreviation for the Ministry of Defence
PE, physical education, is school gym class

explanation.surface: An exercise bike sits in the gym at a government department.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a low-powered motorbike with pedals, a kind of bike.

clue.text: Triple harp enthrals composer

indicators.note: to enthral is literally to hold captive, so the phrase holds the answer within it

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A three-row harp captivates a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple harp is a Welsh harp with three rows of strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár was the Hungarian composer of operettas such as The Merry Widow.

clue.text: Relating to a city, one in South Africa daughter's vacated

indicators.note: something that has vacated a place has moved out of it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Durban is a city in South Africa
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter has moved out of a South African city.
explanation.walkthrough: With D gone from DURBAN, URBAN remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban is the adjective for towns and cities, as opposed to rural.

clue.text: Local shield thrown out

parts.note: a local is a person's nearest or regular pub

indicators.note: something thrown is tossed about, so these letters land in a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood shield, perhaps a trophy, has been thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a local is your regular pub. Out is the definition: a book that is out is in print.
explanation.definitionFit: A book or record that is out has been released to the public, which is what printed and issued means.

clue.text: Given medical attention and not asked to pay

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cared for by a doctor
second meaning: had a meal or drink bought by someone else

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a patient seen free of charge; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both nursing a patient and paying for someone else's food or entertainment.

clue.text: I leave Russia's capital with Russian boy

parts.note: taken as written
to leave is to go

indicators.note: a capital letter is the one at the head of a word, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Russia

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are leaving Moscow with a Russian lad.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital suggests Moscow, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor is a common Russian male first name, so it serves as an example of a boy from Russia.
